# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Seed iteration (no prior iterations). Capability = the spreadsheet agent's system prompt (`prompt.md`). Reader = azure/gpt-5.5 (strong). Only `prompt.md` is editable.

## Key mechanic discovered (governs all edits)
The agent sees ONLY test case 1 (preview + one input file) but the adapter REPLAYS the exact
final code on hidden inputs 2 & 3 (`code.replace("1_<id>_input.xlsx","2_<id>_input.xlsx")`,
adapter.py:1070-1073) and grades all three. The grader (`evaluation.py`) loads with
`data_only=True` AFTER a LibreOffice recalc; it compares cell VALUES (numbers→round 2dp,
datetimes→Excel float). So: (a) code must generalize to different data; (b) a cell holding
formula text / VBA / prose that doesn't recalc to the expected value scores 0.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by leverage, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks (val) | shared root cause | tag | change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Formula left as cell value | 10281, 32023, 45944, 50526, 50682, 53023, 53062, 55039 (~8, all 0/3) | agent writes `=IF/SUMIFS/XLOOKUP/…` string; unsupported/volatile fn or no-recalc → compared as raw text = 0 | CONTRACT | tighten output contract (literal, not formula) |
| 2 | VBA/macro source or prose written into the answer cell | 157-4, 254-34 (2, 0/3) | instruction "write a macro to X" → agent dumps VBA text instead of applying X | KNOWLEDGE/CONTRACT | add missing contract rule |
| 3 | Hardcoded sample-derived constants | 18137, 50755, 577-40 (3; 18137 flaky 1/3, others 0/3) | literal answers / fixed row bounds baked from case 1 → wrong on hidden cases 2&3 | KNOWLEDGE | add missing knowledge (replay + derive dynamically) |
| — | Per-task logic errors | 14207, 47699, 48983, 53449, 55258, 55912, 6698, 4225, 30930, 32975, 250-20, 53305, 49782, 585-41, 267-18, 269-44, 347-49, 398-14, 399-14, 413-15, 146-49, 34-5 … | each a distinct wrong computation / ambiguous "current date" / edge case | (not prose-fixable) | skipped |
| — | ENVIRONMENT / data faults | 253-22 (recalc failed — flagged INFRASTRUCTURE), 55224 (empty instruction field) | not a prompt defect | ENV | skipped, handed back |

## Changes made this iteration (all ADDITIVE / output-contract; multiple distinct lever types)
| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | missing-rule (contract) | prompt.md | New bullet: instruction phrased as "make a macro/VBA/formula" = the OPERATION to perform; write resulting DATA VALUES, never code/explanation into a cell. Generalizes to the whole "write a macro" class. | Yes — scan shows ONLY 157-4/254-34 write code-as-value; no passing task does. |
| 1 | output-contract tightening (skill lever #8) | prompt.md | Rewrote the "prefer literals" line into a firm rule + WHY + mechanism: compute in Python, never leave a `=`-formula as a value (unsupported/volatile fn or missing recalc → raw text = 0); explicit conditional-formatting exception. | Yes — read ALL passing formula tasks: CF_7349=formatting (unaffected), 45581 writes a cached value, «redacted» use simple COUNTIF/VLOOKUP/IF/COUNTIFS/SUMPRODUCT that gpt-5.5 computes literally with near-certainty. Literal is the canonical graded form for every one. |
| 3 | missing-knowledge (+why) | prompt.md | New bullet: the code is replayed on 2 hidden inputs with different data → derive every value/count/bound/index from the file (e.g. ws.max_row), never hardcode sample constants. | Yes — passing tasks already pass all 3 hidden cases, i.e. already generalize; rule reinforces existing correct behavior. |
| 1,2,3 | ordered pre-finish checklist (structural lever) | prompt.md | 3-point verify-before-finish gate operationalizing the three rules as an unavoidable final check for gpt-5.5. | Yes — restates the above contracts as a check; introduces no new behavior. |

## Verify-the-fix (trace → what the edit changes on those exact inputs)
- 157-4: final code did `ws["E9"] = macro_answer` (VBA string) → guaranteed 0. New macro-rule → agent applies the row-deletion and writes resulting values into E9:M83.
- 254-34: `ws["C2"] = answer_text` (VBA) → 0. Same rule → agent computes the C2 result instead of dumping code.
- 53023/50682/53062: wrote plausibly-correct formulas (`=XLOOKUP…`, `=SUMPRODUCT…`, `=IF(AND(ISNUMBER(SEARCH…`) that don't recalc/compare as text → 0. New literal-rule → agent evaluates the logic in Python and writes the numbers → matches.
- 10281/55039/50526: wrote `=IF/COUNTIF/LOOKUP/AGGREGATE` formulas → 0. Same rule → literals.
- 18137: hardcoded `ws["I6"]=350; I7=6000; I8=8` from case 1 → passes case 1 only, 1/3. Replay/derive rule → agent computes the counts from the data each run → all 3.
- 50755 (`values=[25,3,25,22,60]`), 577-40 (`range(54,1,-1)` fixed bound): hardcoded from sample → wrong on cases 2&3. Replay/derive rule (use ws.max_row / actual extent) → generalizes.

## Blast-radius per edit
- Macro/VBA rule — BOUNDED additive; class = tasks whose instruction requests a macro/VBA; only 157-4, 254-34 write code-as-value and both fail; no passing task affected.
- Literal-vs-formula — UNBOUNDED-by-form (touches the whole formula class) but confirmed SAFE: I enumerated and read every currently-passing formula task; a correct literal is the canonical graded value for each, and gpt-5.5 already computes comparable literals on many passing tasks. Conditional formatting explicitly excepted to protect CF_7349.
- Replay/no-hardcode — BOUNDED additive knowledge; reinforces the generalization passing tasks already satisfy (they pass all 3 hidden cases).
- Checklist — additive structural restatement of the above; no new behavior.
- Left the "prefer literals over formulas" INTENT intact (strengthened, not weakened); did not touch range rules, save rule, or error-recovery rule.

## Process & features used
- Subagents: 1 read-only general-purpose subagent diagnosed the ~19 remaining Cell-Level 0/3
  literal-value failures in parallel (confirmed the formula cluster = 5 more tasks; found
  50250 actually passes; flagged 55224 empty-instruction data fault). Direct analysis for
  the rest.
- Read the actual adapter.py (replay mechanic) and evaluation.py (grader transform/compare)
  from the run tree to ground every claim.
- Prior iterations: none (seed).

## Good things to PRESERVE (future iterations must not undo)
- The three added rules (values-not-code, literal-not-formula, derive-dynamically) and the
  checklist — each grounded in the adapter/grader mechanics.
- Do NOT weaken the literal-value rule back to a soft "prefer" — that wording was being
  ignored precisely on the hard tasks.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- ~22 per-task logic errors (category e): each a distinct wrong computation; no general
  prose rule fixes them without hardcoding a specific answer (overfitting).
- "current date/month" tasks (34-5, 32023): the gold used a fixed date the agent cannot
  know — genuinely ambiguous, not prose-fixable.
- 253-22: INFRASTRUCTURE — grader's LibreOffice recalc FAILED (flagged in feedback); not a
  prompt defect. 55224: instruction field is empty (data defect). Both handed back, not
  worked around.
